name: LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS SurgeonSight Precision-3
description:
The SurgeonSight Precision-3 is a medical-grade full-replacement ocular engineered specifically for high-precision surgical and clinical environments, offering optical zoom from 0.5x wide-field to 40x microsurgical magnification with sub-micron focal stability. The integrated tissue analysis overlay uses near-infrared spectroscopy to display live vascularization maps, tissue oxygenation gradients, and anomalous cellular density flagging directly in the visual field. Depth-perception calibration is performed during installation to the individual surgeon's neural signature, ensuring that spatial judgment under magnification remains accurate rather than disorienting.

The Precision-3 is the standard of care in GLMZ's Tier 4-5 hospital systems and the preferred ocular of the city's elite surgical corps — cardiovascular specialists, microsurgeons, and the rare neural-reconstruction practitioners who work in the Spire's private clinics. Lazarus sells them at a price point that keeps them firmly out of Shelf-level reach, which has created a gray market of older Precision-2 units circulating among unlicensed street docs who use them for everything from trauma triage to illegal augmentation installation.
installation_requirements: Full ocular extraction; calibration procedure requiring 4-hour neural mapping session; Lazarus-certified medical installer only
rejection_risk: Minimal — Lazarus biocompatible coating and proprietary rejection-minimizing gel matrix; lowest rejection rate in class
maintenance: Bi-annual spectroscopy sensor recalibration; annual neural signature re-sync; lens array inspection every 3 months
specifications: {"zoom_range": "0.5x to 40x", "focal_stability": "sub-micron at max magnification", "tissue_analysis": "near-infrared spectroscopy overlay", "vein_mapping": "real-time vascularization display", "oxygenation_monitoring": "live tissue O2 gradient", "anomaly_flagging": "cellular density deviation >2 sigma", "depth_calibration": "individual neural signature", "recording": "optional 8K surgical log", "power": "bioelectric passive draw, 200hr standby"}
side_effects: Zoom reflex triggering — involuntary magnification when focusing on fine detail in daily life, causing momentary disorientation
Tissue overlay persistence in off-duty contexts — wearers begin involuntarily analyzing skin and tissue on strangers
Prolonged use at high magnification causes headaches in roughly 15% of users until neural adaptation completes
Emotional detachment reported by long-term surgical users — the analytical overlay bleeds into interpersonal perception
cultural_context: In GLMZ's medical community, a surgeon without Precision-3s is quietly considered a liability — the eyes have become so standard in elite surgical practice that hospitals now factor ocular spec into credentialing reviews. Among Shelf-level street docs, a salvaged pair of Precision-2s is worth more than most people's annual income and carries the weight of a credential they'll never officially hold.
known_users: Elite cardiovascular and microsurgeons in Tier 4-5 hospital systems
Unlicensed street surgeons operating with salvaged older units
Forensic pathologists and high-precision lab technicians
story_hooks: A Precision-3 unit recovered from a murdered surgeon still contains an encrypted surgical log of a procedure that was never officially performed — on a patient listed as never admitted
A street doc's salvaged Precision-2 begins displaying tissue anomaly flags on every person they look at — the spectroscopy sensor is malfunctioning, or something in the water is wrong

Lazarus Pharmaceuticals issues a silent recall on all Precision-3 units manufactured in a specific 6-month window — no explanation given, and surgeons who comply are left blind during the replacement wait
